slides.title: Direct Your Career Deliberately, Not by Chance
bullets: A development plan is a deliberate map for actively directing your own growth
The alternative is leaving progression to chance opportunities or others' decisions
Building your own plan turns this course into a personal, actionable roadmap

slides.title: Start With an Honest Self-Assessment
bullets: Assess yourself honestly against every competency built across this course
Scientific exchange, insight capture, critical thinking, evidence generation, congress execution
Strategic planning, digital fluency, AI use, and leadership
Identify where you're already solid and where a real gap exists

slides.title: Set Specific, Time-Bound Goals
bullets: Replace generic goals like improve my leadership skills with specific, measurable ones
Apply the same rigor used for strategic imperatives earlier in the course
Example: lead the next two post-congress debriefs and request explicit feedback on executive synthesis

slides.title: Identify Concrete Development Pathways
bullets: Structured training and mentoring from a more senior professional
Active participation in cross-functional projects to practice influence without authority
Deliberately seeking higher-visibility opportunities like an executive presentation or committee role

slides.title: Review the Plan Periodically
bullets: Reassess progress against your goals every few months
Adjust the plan based on what you've learned
Incorporate new priorities as your trajectory and the organization's needs evolve

slides.title: A Living Tool, Not an Archived Document
bullets: A development plan only works if actively maintained, not filed away
This is what turns course knowledge into a sustained trajectory of growth and impact

takeaway.title: A development plan turns this course's content into your own actionable career roadmap
bullets: Honest self-assessment against real competencies is the starting point
Specific, time-bound goals beat generic aspirations
Periodic review keeps the plan a living tool, not an archived document
